en_summary: US companies are facing a massive debt maturity wall: ~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corporate bonds and loans mature over the next 5 years, including $438 billion due by the end of 2028. Junk-rated debt maturing within 2 years surged +31% YoY. $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt due by 2031. Refinancing expensive, effective yield on US junk debt +150 bps to 8.0% over last 12 months. Corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.
text:
US companies are facing a massive debt maturity wall:

~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corporate bonds and loans mature over the next 5 years, including $438 billion due by the end of 2028.

By comparison, in 2020, 2021, and 2022, this figure ranged from $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion.

The amount of junk-rated debt maturing within 2 years alone has surged +31% YoY.

At the same time, $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt is coming due by 2031.

Meanwhile, refinancing is becoming increasingly expensive, with the effective yield on publicly issued US junk debt rising +150 basis points over the last 12 months, to 8.0%.

The corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.

A lot of the top enterprises are not letting their employees use this in an unconstrained fashion, and they're certainly not letting them connect their email, their knowledge bases, their Notions, their Slacks.

Big corporations are not letting people actually use the power of AI because they're scared about cyber.

The sizing ranged from Vega neutral to single stock book (which collected theta) to theta neutral which was Vega long. 

The drop in implied correlation makes the trade less attractive.  But given the level of implied on index the notable risk isn't selling index vol to low its buying single name vol way way too high. Remember the boiler room pump-and-dump schemes of the 2000s, where brokers would sell garbage stocks at massive markups? The same thing happened with garbage bonds in the ’90s. A lot of folks today look back and chuckle, asking, “Who would be dumb enough to fall for that?” To them, these were clearly horrible investments and outright grifts.

This is exactly what QIS is in today’s era. Banks charge a markup on absolute garbage strategies that never work, then rotate them in and out every few months with a “new idea” after the old one breaks.

There are hundreds of billions of dollars in these horrible programs across almost every tier-one platform. It’s very sad to see pensions and other institutions blow capital on this type of stuff.

text:
Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way .

@robin_j_brooks is correct in this analysis. This is a regime shift, not a blip.

For most of 2026, oil up meant yields up. Inflation expectations fed straight into the long end. That link is now broken. The 20-day correlation between Brent and the 10Y has collapsed to its lowest since late 2024.

The reason is Europe. The French 10-year is at 4.96%, the highest since 2002. The spread over German Bunds has widened to 159bp, the widest since 2011. French debt-to-GDP is 117%, versus 90% at the last crisis peak.

Bessent confirmed this week that capital is leaving "concerning" jurisdictions and flowing into Treasuries as a safe haven. The US is catching a bid because the alternative is worse.

This is not a resolution of the fiscal problem. Net interest is still above $1 trillion. The term premium is being temporarily suppressed by a flight to quality, not by better US math.

If Europe stabilizes, the bid fades. If Europe cracks, the bid deepens.

en_summary: I think one of most overlooked parts of $TSLA and $SPCX is how they're already building what could become one massive AI infrastructure ecosystem. text:
Binance lost about $6.3 billion in Thursday's hack. It is the largest crypto theft on record in dollar terms, roughly four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The drain started at 4:05 PM ET on Oct 29. TRM Labs says most of it left Binance wallets in about 20 minutes, across 10 blockchains.

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover users. $5 billion of that is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen, about 80% of the loss. It is buying the rest through the market and OTC desks.

About $3 billion has been frozen on-chain, almost all of it $USDT and $USDC. The attacker still holds 18,270 $BTC split across 19 wallets. Elliptic says none of it has reached an exchange or service yet.

TRM and Chainalysis attribute the theft with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit. No government has confirmed it. Trump on Friday: "We don't know. We're looking at that." The FBI and Secret Service are both involved.

TRM counts $12.8 billion stolen by North Korea since 2017. $7.4 billion of it came this year.

Binance is targeting a phased restart of withdrawals early Sunday. Proof of reserves results are due Monday.

Dan Held says the price gap between crypto exchanges isn't arbitrage, but a premium traders are paid for taking on counterparty risk

"I was talking to some arbitrage traders in crypto, and I'm like, you're not arbitraging anything."

"What you are arbing is the exchange counterparty risk, because you're putting funds at risk, and there's a small premium or discount because of that risk."

"To do that trade, you have to have funds on every exchange at all times. Both the token that you're trying to arbitrage and dollars of some sort."

"We saw this with Mt. Gox and Bitstamp. Back in the day, coins on Mt. Gox traded higher than Bitstamp. The reason why is that Mt. Gox's fiat legs, the ability to wire money out, had withdrawal issues. The only way to get your money out was to buy Bitcoin."

"And what we learned is that there's no arbitrage at all there. It was counterparty risk."

en_summary: Cataclysmic session on Wall Street. AI demand holds but financing cracks: Anthropic reportedly not investment grade post-IPO with over $800B compute commitments to 2045. Hyperscalers and $AVGO continue to carry the load while $NVDA discusses guarantee on Nscale. Semis pricing peak capex though neither capex nor ARR slowing much. SOX -10%, $INTC crushed -30% worst day since 1974, $NVDA -5%, Mag7 limited damage. Much demand pulled forward. Part of the drop is mechanical like 2020 (CTAs, vol targeting, SOXL rebalancing). Looks like violent rotation out of tech rather than general equity flight. Next catalyst is Anthropic October ARR, IPO and OpenAI raise. AI infrastructure thesis unchanged but volatility is the price. By @Frenchie_.

Séance cataclysmique sur Wall Street

Si vous êtes investi dans l'IA vous voulez peut-être vous asseoir avant de lire ça

Quelques explications :

A/ On l’apprend il y a une heure, Anthropic ne serait pas investment grade après l’IPO, avec plus de 800 Md$ de compute engagés jusqu’en 2045, c'est une très mauvaise news

B/ Les hyperscalers et $AVGO vont devoir continuer à porter la note pendant que $NVDA discute d’une garantie sur Nscale

>$INTC pulvérisé à -30 %, pire jour depuis 1974
>$NVDA cope avec -5 %, les Mag7 limitent la casse

CTA qui vendent la cassure de tendance, fonds à volatilité cible qui coupent quand ça bouge trop, multi-stratégies qui réduisent tout leur book, et ETF à levier genre le SOXL qui doivent vendre en clôture pour rester à 3x
